answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to escrow a stake and solve tasks checked by peers. Reputation rises only when answers match verified outcomes; colluding clones cannot cheaply manufacture that signal, because disagreement or duplicate behavior triggers slashing. To flood a network, an attacker must fund every fake identity and lose stakes when it fails, so cost scales with the number of Sybils. At zenith demand, the ocean of collateral makes imitation uneconomic.
